questions.question: Which exact RDKit routine and optimization settings does GUIDEMOL use to generate 3D structures from SMILES?

options.A: EmbedMolecule with ETKDGv3 followed by UFF for 500 iterations
options.C: ConstrainedEmbed followed by MMFF94s for 1000 iterations
options.D: AddHs followed by Chem.rdDistGeom with a 5000 kcal/mol cutoff

questions.rationale: The paper names the optimization call, force-field variant and iteration limit.
questions.evidence_quote: The 3D molecular models are obtained with the RDKit function MMFFOptimizeMolecule and the arguments mmffVariant='MMFF94' and maxIters=5000.

questions.question: Which preprocessing choices can be applied before generating the models from SMILES?

options.A: Remove metals, retain the largest preferably organic fragment, and neutralize
options.B: Aromatize rings, retain only the smallest fragment, and protonate all heteroatoms
options.C: Remove salts, force a single tautomer, and assign MMFF atom types
options.D: Neutralize, canonicalize stereochemistry, and delete all explicit hydrogens

questions.rationale: The three listed optional steps are metal disconnection, largest-fragment selection, and uncharging.
questions.evidence_quote: to remove metals (based on the MetalDisconnector class), to keep the largest fragment (uses LargestFragmentChooser(preferOrganic=True)), or to neutralize (uses Uncharger).

questions.question: Which descriptor families are explicitly exposed from RDKit's rdMolDescriptors module in the interface?

options.A: RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, GETAWAY, PEOE_VSA and SMR_VSA
options.B: Morgan, MACCS, Avalon, ErG, AtomPair and TopologicalTorsion
options.C: BCUT, Kappa, Chi, Hall-Kier, LabuteASA and EState
options.D: RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, PEOE_VSA, Morgan and MACCS

questions.rationale: These are the seven listed 3D descriptor families; exact molecular weight is separately selectable.
questions.evidence_quote: RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, GETAWAY, PEOE_VSA and SMR_VSA.

questions.question: In the electrostatic-potential grid, how are atoms very close to a cube center treated in the stated equation?

options.A: They are excluded when r<1 Å, and their contribution equals their partial charge
options.B: They are retained with a Coulomb term capped at 1/r=1 Å
options.C: They are assigned zero charge and excluded only if also beyond the cutoff
options.D: They are replaced by their atomic number before potential summation

questions.rationale: The method excludes atoms at distance less than 1 Å from the cube center while specifying their contribution as their partial charge.
questions.evidence_quote: the atoms at a distance < 1 Å from the center of the cube (the contribution is equal to its partial charge)

questions.question: Which pair of user-set spatial parameters is used to specify a potential-grid calculation, in addition to the cutoff?

options.A: Grid-center coordinates and side length, with cube size setting resolution
options.B: Molecular centroid and atom count, with a fixed 1 Å voxel width
options.C: Grid origin and number of molecules, with sigma controlling resolution
options.D: Center-of-mass coordinates and dielectric constant, with side length setting cutoff

questions.rationale: Users set the center coordinates, grid side size, and cube size; the cutoff determines which distant atoms contribute.
questions.evidence_quote: The coordinates of the center of the grid, the size of each side (in Angstrom) and the size of the cube are also defined by the user.

questions.question: How does GUIDEMOL form each voxel-grid value from atom-specific properties?

options.A: It sums pᵢ exp(−rᵢc²/(2σ²)) over atoms within the cutoff
options.B: It averages pᵢ/rᵢc over all atoms and normalizes by molecular mass
options.C: It sums pᵢ exp(−rᵢc/(2σ)) over atoms closer than 1 Å
options.D: It assigns the nearest atom's property, then smooths by a Coulomb kernel

questions.rationale: The voxel representation uses a Gaussian distance weighting of the selected atomic property and omits atoms beyond the cutoff.
questions.evidence_quote: VoxG c = ∑ i=1 N p i ×exp ( -r ic 2 2 σ 2 )

questions.question: Which set consists entirely of atomic properties implemented for voxelization?

options.A: Element atomic number, partial charge, and Wildman–Crippen atomic contributions to refractivity and logP
options.B: Element atomic number, electronegativity, polarizability and Gasteiger–Marsili bond order
options.C: Partial charge, atomic mass, solvent-accessible area and topological degree
options.D: MMFF energy, refractivity, aromaticity and molecular dipole contribution

questions.rationale: The implementation supports atomic number, Gasteiger/MMFF charge, and Crippen refractivity/logP contributions.
questions.evidence_quote: Implemented properties are the atomic number of the element, the partial atomic charge (Gasteiger or MMFF) and atomic contributions to molecular refractivity and logP using the Wildman-Crippen approach

questions.question: What limitation did the authors report for selected 3D descriptors across repeated runs or operating systems?

options.A: Some GETAWAY, MORSE and WHIM values differed despite the same RDKit version and generated structure
options.B: All RDF and PEOE_VSA values changed because GUIDEMOL randomized atomic charges
options.C: Only exact molecular weight varied because the GUI rounded masses by operating system
options.D: Voxel and potential grids were nondeterministic, while every RDKit descriptor remained invariant

questions.rationale: They observed non-reproducibility for some listed 3D descriptors under the same RDKit version.
questions.evidence_quote: for some molecules, and some GETAWAY, MORSE and WHIM descriptors, different values were obtained with the same RDKit version (2022.9.5) in different runs or in different operating systems.

questions.question: When hydrogens are added to an existing 3D input structure, what coordinate-handling behavior does the option specify?

options.A: Hydrogen coordinates are generated without changing other atoms' coordinates, using AddHs(addCoords=True)
options.B: All atoms are re-embedded, with existing heavy-atom coordinates used only as restraints
options.C: Hydrogens are placed at idealized positions and the structure is subsequently minimized
options.D: Only hydrogens missing from aromatic groups are added, with coordinates left undefined

questions.rationale: The optional operation adds missing H coordinates while leaving the supplied atoms unmoved.
questions.evidence_quote: The descriptors are calculated from the 3D structure supplied by the user. However, an option is available for the addition of missing hydrogen atoms, for which the 3D coordinates are calculated without changing the coordinates of the other atoms

questions.question: What does the article say about the BSD license and intended extensibility of GUIDEMOL?

options.A: Its three-clause BSD license permits commercial and non-commercial use, and the source can be adapted for other descriptors or GUI tasks
options.B: Its GPL license requires all derived descriptor workflows to be open source
options.C: Its research-only license permits classroom use but forbids commercial modification
options.D: Its BSD license allows descriptor calculations but prohibits reuse of the tkinter interface

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly describe both the license scope and the code's adaptability.
questions.evidence_quote: under the three-clause Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD) license, which allows both commercial and non-commercial use, and can be very easily extended for the deployment of other molecular descriptors
